dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقابِرَ): «ألهاكم التكاثر» is a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and a fāʿil (agent) placed after. «التكاثر» is vying in abundance and boasting of it; the «ال» in «التكاثر» is for the known reference (li-l-ʿahd), namely vying in [the goods of] this world and its pleasures, and the marvels and dazzling sights that appear in it, which captivate the beholder and deceive him for a time. «حتى» may be a conjunction, and may be a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; in either case it stands as the limit of the distraction. «زرتم المقابر» is a past verb, its agent and its direct object. What is meant by the visiting is boasting of the dead, i.e. giddiness and folly have brought you to a point that led you to visit the graves; or: to vying in wealth you added visiting the graves, so as to vie in [the number of] the dead. It is also permissible that the meaning be: vying in wealth and children distracted you until you died and were buried, having wasted your lives on what has no profit in it, and having neglected and lost what is more important and more beneficial, namely striving for your Hereafter. In that case the visiting of the graves is an expression for death, and «حتى» must be the genitive-governing «حتى» of limit.
(كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ): «كلا» is a particle of deterrence and rebuke against being occupied away from acts of obedience and inclining to ornaments and outward appearances; «سوف» is a particle of the future; «تعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. «ثم» is a conjunction, and «سوف تعلمون» is conjoined to the first clause. Ibn Mālik made it a case of verbal tawkīd (emphasis) with a conjunction intervening. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The repetition is an emphasis of the deterrence and the warning, and "ثم" indicates that the second warning is more forceful and severe than the first, as you say to one being advised: I tell you, and then I tell you: do not do it.» The apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted, i.e. if you knew the terror that lies before you, you would do what cannot be described or fathomed — but they are ignorant and astray. «تعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the wāw is the agent, and the object is omitted, its implied form being "the outcome of distraction, boasting and vying for more". «علم اليقين» is a maṣdar (verbal noun); it is said that its origin is «العلم اليقين», so it is a case of annexing the qualified noun to its qualifier. Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: «And "عين اليقين" is a maṣdar according to the meaning, because raʾā and ʿāyana have one meaning.» It is not correct for His saying «لترون» to be the apodosis [of «لو»], because its occurrence is certain, so it is not made conditional. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «ترون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, [which is] omitted because of the succession of identical letters. Its origin is «لترأيون»: when the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, it was changed to alif, and it was dropped because of its being quiescent along with the quiescence of the wāw after it; then the vowel of the hamza, which is the ʿayn (second radical) of the word, was cast onto the rāʾ, and [the hamza] was dropped because of its heaviness; then the doubled nūn of emphasis came in, so the nūn of the nominative was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, as we stated before, and the wāw was vowelled with ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was not dropped because, had it been dropped, the verb would have been impaired by the loss of its ʿayn, its lām (third radical) and the wāw of the pronoun.
(ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ): conjoined to what preceded. «عين اليقين» is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «you will surely see it with a seeing [that is] the very eye of certainty»; the seeing, which is the cause of certainty, was described as being the very eye of certainty.
(ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ): also conjoined. «تسألن» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, [which is] omitted because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the agent was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. «يومئذ» and «عن النعيم» are attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تسألن». The emphatic intensifications are six; they will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
This sūra contains intensification (mubālagha) in six ways, which we set out below:
1- Repetition of the warning, to indicate that the second warning is more forceful than the first, in His saying «ثم كلا سوف تعلمون».
2- Repetition of the alert: He said «لو تعلمون» with the apodosis omitted, so that the imagination may go every way in supplying it; we have set it out for you in the i'rab.
3- The oath in His saying «لترون الجحيم», to emphasise the threat.
4- He repeated the oath, conjoined with «ثم», in His saying «ثم لترونها عين اليقين», to make the threat more severe and the menace greater.
5- Making the seeing «the very eye of certainty» and its pure essence is a particular intensification.
6- He repeated the oath, conjoined with «ثم», in His saying «ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم». If you say: what is the bliss about which man is questioned and reproached, when there is no one who does not have some bliss? I say: it is the bliss of the idle and the boastful, who have inclined to pleasures and hastened into sins, and have exhausted their time in amusement, merriment and the open fields of pleasure, desiring no substitute for them and sending forth nothing for their world or their Hereafter. So the «ال» in «النعيم» is for comprehensiveness (al-istighrāq).
